items.title: Anthem Owes $854K For No Surprises Act Awards, Court Told - law360.com
items.reason: This item directly addresses No Surprises Act litigation and enforcement, reporting a specific court determination of financial liability for a major insurer's compliance failures.
items.summary: A court has determined that Anthem owes $854,000 in No Surprises Act-related awards, according to Law360 reporting on litigation enforcement. The case represents a concrete court judgment regarding insurer compliance with federal balance-billing protections and the No Surprises Act's requirements. This ruling directly impacts Anthem's financial obligations under the law and signals judicial enforcement of No Surprises Act requirements against major insurers. Revenue-cycle teams should monitor this precedent as it demonstrates potential liability exposure for non-compliant balance-billing practices and IDR-related failures.

items.title: No Surprises Act dispute process has increased medical costs by $22.4 billion over four years - Substack
items.reason: This item directly addresses the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process and its financial impact on healthcare costs, which is central to NSA implementation and revenue-cycle operations.
items.summary: A Substack analysis claims the No Surprises Act's dispute resolution process has contributed to a $22.4 billion increase in medical costs over four years. The article appears to examine the financial consequences of the IDR (Independent Dispute Resolution) process, which is the mechanism established under the NSA for resolving payment disputes between providers and insurers when balance-billing disagreements arise. This finding is material to revenue-cycle teams because it quantifies potential cost pressures and efficiency challenges within the NSA framework that directly affects claim dispute handling, payment determinations, and operational expenses related to the federal balance-billing protections implemented under the law.

items.title: Maryland sues UnitedHealthcare alleging they provided faulty software that cost taxpayers millions - Tri-State Alert
items.reason: This is a state attorney general enforcement action against a major payer (UnitedHealthcare) alleging software failures that caused financial harm, which directly fits the litigation and regulatory enforcement category of the topic definition.
items.summary: Maryland has sued UnitedHealthcare, alleging the company provided faulty software that resulted in millions of dollars in costs to taxpayers. The lawsuit represents a state regulatory enforcement action against a major national payer for allegedly deficient technology systems. This action is relevant to revenue-cycle teams as it reflects state-level scrutiny of payer operational practices and systems that affect claim processing and administrative integrity. The case may influence expectations for payer software quality and accountability across state Medicaid programs.

items.title: BCBS lawsuit over CVS generic drug prices moves forward - BenefitsPRO
items.reason: This involves litigation against a major payer (BCBS) over drug pricing practices, which falls squarely within payer enforcement and litigation scope, though the article excerpt is minimal.
items.summary: A lawsuit against Blue Cross Blue Shield (BCBS) concerning CVS generic drug prices is progressing through the legal system. The litigation appears to challenge BCBS pricing practices or contract terms related to generic drugs supplied by CVS, directly implicating payer claims-processing and reimbursement decisions that affect revenue-cycle operations. The outcome could establish precedent for how payers must handle generic drug pricing and contracting, impacting formulary compliance, claims adjudication, and provider reimbursement rates.
